newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada postal workers vote to authorize strike.
newsitem.headline: Canada postal workers vote to authorize strike.

text.p: The union representing Canada's 45,000 postal workers has voted to strike if it does not reach an agreement with Canada Post by the middle of August.
Members of the Canadian Union of Postal Workers voted 89.5 percent in favor of strike action, the union said on Friday.
Canadian postal workers have a history of long and unsettling labor disputes with Canada Post, a federal government-owned Crown corporation.
The main obstacles to an agreement were job security and wages, union president Darrell Tingley said in a statement.
"No agreement is possible if Canada Post continues to be intransigent on such vital issues as job security, wages and work rules," Tingley said.
Canada Post did not immediately return calls for comment.
The two sides are scheduled to return to the bargaining table on July 14.
If there was no agreement by the middle of August, the postal workers would likely be in a legal strike position by the end of August or early September, the union said.
The parties began negotiations in April but talks broke off after six weeks, the union said.
